basic_information.official_title: AN ACT AMENDING BANGSAMORO AUTONOMY ACT NO. 35, ENTITLED “AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE BANGSAMORO ELECTORAL CODE OF THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO”
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Rewrites the rules for the region's first parliamentary election — who may form a party, how party and sectoral seats are won, and a ₱500 million appropriation to run the vote. Every existing party certification is cancelled and must be sought afresh.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: The act states no separate purpose. It amends the Bangsamoro Electoral Code ahead of the first BARMM Parliamentary Election, tightening party requirements and rebuilding the sectoral certification process.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: Regional parties need 5,000 members and chapters in every province and city. Parties need 2.5% of the vote to win party seats. All sectoral certifications are revoked and must be re-obtained under a new 15-day process. ₱500 million goes to COMELEC.
who_will_be_affected: Every voter in the first BARMM parliamentary election
Regional political parties and coalitions, all of which must re-register
Sectoral organisations, whose certifications are cancelled outright
Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples, who elect their representative by sectoral assembly
Incumbent BTA members intending to run
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force from 2026 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. If you belong to a party or a sectoral organisation, your accreditation is cancelled and you must apply again. Parties need 2.5% of the vote to win a seat, and at least 30% of their nominees must be women.
in_practice: A regional political party needs at least 5,000 members who are residents and registered voters, distributed across a majority of provinces and cities
Every party must have provincial and city chapters in all provinces and cities, and municipal chapters in a majority of municipalities
Registration requires a notarised list of at least 5,000 members with names and signatures
At least 30% of a party's nominees must be women, and as far as practicable one in every three
A party needs at least 2.5% of the total valid votes in the party system election to qualify for party representation seats
All existing sectoral certifications are revoked; a new certification process applies
Certifying ministries must act on a sectoral application within a non-extendible 15 days, and the certification issues automatically if they do not
Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples elect their sectoral representative through their sectoral assembly; other sectors are elected by direct plurality
Only one candidate per accredited organisation for other sectors
₱500,000,000 is appropriated to augment COMELEC's funds, released immediately

for_specific_groups.Women: Section 3 retains the requirement that at least 30% of a regional party's nominees be women — and, as far as practicable, one in every three.
for_specific_groups.Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples: Your sectoral representative is elected by your own sectoral assembly rather than by a general vote — the one sector treated this way.
for_specific_groups.Sectoral organisations: Every certification previously issued is revoked and cancelled. You must go through the new process, and the ministry has a non-extendible 15 days to decide.
for_specific_groups.Political parties: All existing parties, organisations and coalitions must register and seek new accreditation. Failure to do so bars you from the election. COMELEC allows no more than 60 days after the rules are issued.
for_specific_groups.Incumbent BTA members: Filing a Certificate of Candidacy does not make you ipso facto resigned, and Members designated to Cabinet or executive offices are likewise not deemed resigned.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: The BARMM, for the first Bangsamoro parliamentary election and after.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: At the first BARMM Parliamentary Election, whose date is determined by the Philippine Congress.
what_you_can_do: If you run a sectoral organisation, start the new certification process — your old certificate no longer exists
If you are in a political party, check it has re-registered with COMELEC through the BRAC within the 60-day window
Hold a certifying ministry to the 15-day deadline: the certification issues on lapse unless there is justifiable cause, and failure to act is a ground for disciplinary action
Ask COMELEC for the implementing rules, due within 30 days of effectivity
watch_out_for: Requiring chapters in every province and city, plus a majority of municipalities, is a high organisational bar that favours large established parties.
The blanket revocation of all sectoral certifications resets the field shortly before the first election.
Appointed BTA members may run without resigning, and may hold Cabinet posts while doing so.
The act repeals 5 sections of the Electoral Code (Sections 31–35) without restating what they contained.
The date of the first election is set by the Philippine Congress, not by the region.

key_terms_explained.Regional political party: A party organised within the Bangsamoro to contest its parliamentary elections.
key_terms_explained.Party representation seats: Seats allocated to parties by share of the vote, separate from district seats.
key_terms_explained.Sectoral representative: A member of Parliament representing a defined sector rather than a geographical district.
key_terms_explained.BRAC: Bangsamoro Registration and Accreditation Committee, which accredits organisations fielding sectoral candidates.
key_terms_explained.Ipso facto resigned: Automatically treated as having resigned — which, under this act, filing a candidacy does not trigger for BTA members.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Sha'ban 09, 1447 / 28 January 2026, approved by Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua on 11 February 2026.

benefits.headline: Clear thresholds, a women's quota retained, and a deadline that certifying ministries cannot let slip.

direct_benefits.benefit: At least 30% of party nominees must be women
Automatic certification if a ministry misses the 15-day deadline
Disciplinary liability for officials who fail to act in time
Self-determination of the Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples' representative
direct_benefits.how_to_access: Election by their own sectoral assembly under Section 8

direct_benefits.benefit: ₱500,000,000 for the conduct of the first parliamentary election

indirect_benefits: A written 2.5% threshold, so party seat allocation is predictable
Required written reasons before a certification is denied
limitations: High organisational thresholds for new parties.
Only one candidate per accredited organisation for other sectors.

for_parties: Register and seek new accreditation with COMELEC through the BRAC within the period allowed
Maintain at least 5,000 member-voters and the required provincial, city and municipal chapters
Ensure at least 30% of nominees are women
for_sectoral_organisations: Undergo the new certification process — submit a verified petition, member list, constitution and by-laws, and sector platform

what_is_prohibited: Participating in the electoral process without securing accreditation under the new requirements — failure to do so bars a party from taking part.
Fielding more than one candidate per accredited organisation for other sectors.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment for voters.
penalties.for_officials: Failure of a certifying official to act on a sectoral application within the prescribed period is a ground for disciplinary action.
penalties.for_parties: A party that fails to secure accreditation under the new law is barred from participating in the electoral process.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The certifying ministry or office, which must issue internal rules covering motions for reconsideration, appeals and revocation
where_to_complain.oversight: Commission on Elections, through the Bangsamoro Registration and Accreditation Committee
where_to_complain.note: A denial must specify the just cause or legal ground, and cannot be issued without notifying the organisation.

everyday_scenarios: A women's organisation applies for sectoral certification. The ministry has a non-extendible 15 days; if it does not act, the certification issues by operation of the act, and the official who let it lapse faces disciplinary action.

A new party wants to contest the election. It needs 5,000 member-voters spread across a majority of provinces and cities, chapters in every province and city, and municipal chapters in most municipalities.
A Non-Moro Indigenous community wants a say in who represents them. Their representative is elected by their own sectoral assembly, not by a region-wide vote.
An appointed BTA member files a Certificate of Candidacy. Under Section 16 they are not deemed resigned and may keep their position, including a Cabinet post.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Amends Section 1, Article III of BAA 35: a regional political party is established by at least 5,000 members who are residents and registered voters, distributed throughout a majority of the provinces and cities composing the Bangsamoro territory; all parties must establish provincial and city chapters in all provinces and cities and municipal chapters in a majority of the municipalities, and a provincial chapter must have municipal chapters in a majority of that province's municipalities.

Section 2 — Amends Section 4(c): registration requires a notarised list of at least 5,000 members manifesting their collective decision to register the party, with names, signatures and details determined by COMELEC.

Section 3 — Retains Section 9(b): regional political parties shall ensure that at least 30% of party nominees are women, and as far as practicable that at least one in every three nominees is a woman.

Sections 4–5 — Amend Sections 9 and 12 of Article IV(A): party representatives are members of registered regional political parties receiving at least two and one-half percent of the total valid votes cast for the party system election, and only such parties qualify to participate in the allocation of party representation seats.

Section 6 — Process of certification for sectoral organisations and sectoral wings: submission of a verified petition, a verified list of members and officers, constitution and by-laws, and the sector platform, policies, principles and legislative agenda. An incomplete submission is denied outright without prejudice to refiling. The certifying ministry must act within a non-extendible 15 days; the certification issues on lapse of that period unless justifiable cause for denial exists, and no denial may be made without notifying the organisation and specifying the just cause or legal ground. Failure to act within the period is a ground for disciplinary action against the erring official. Ministries issue their own rules on reconsideration, appeals and revocation, which shall not affect the incumbency of a sectoral representative duly elected in the immediately preceding parliamentary election.
Section 7 — All certifications previously issued to sectoral organisations and sectoral wings of political parties are revoked and cancelled, and a new certification process must be undertaken.

Section 8 — Amends Section 17, Article IV(C): except for the Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples, who are elected by their sectoral assembly, sectoral representatives are elected through direct plurality of valid votes cast for the representative sectors. Candidates must be members of a regional political party or an accredited sectoral party or organisation, certified by the appropriate ministry on the basis of their track record in their advocacy. The election of sectoral representatives commences in the first BARMM Parliamentary Election determined by the Philippine Congress.
Section 9 — Candidates for other sectors are fielded by organisations accredited by the Bangsamoro Registration and Accreditation Committee, with only one candidate per accredited organisation.
Sections 10–14 — Repeal Sections 31 and 32 of Article IV(E) and Sections 33, 34 and 35 of Article IV(F) of BAA 35.

Sections 15–16 — Amend the transitory provisions: the election of sectoral representatives, except the NMIPs, is synchronised with the first Parliamentary Elections and automated; and incumbent appointed BTA members whose positions are elective by nature are not deemed ipso facto resigned on filing a Certificate of Candidacy, nor are Members designated to Cabinet and other executive offices.

Section 17 — All existing political parties, organisations and coalitions intending to participate in the first BARMM Parliamentary Election must register and seek new accreditation with COMELEC through the BRAC under the new eligibility requirements; failure to secure accreditation bars a party from participating. COMELEC allows not more than 60 days for compliance after the implementing rules are promulgated.

Section 18 — Appropriates ₱500,000,000 to augment COMELEC's funds for the conduct of the first BARMM Parliamentary Election and the implementation of the act, from any readily available sources of Bangsamoro Government funds, released immediately upon effectivity.
Section 19 — COMELEC shall promulgate implementing rules within 30 days of effectivity.
Section 22 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

who_benefits: Voters in the first parliamentary election

citizen_questions.a: Yes. All existing political parties, organisations and coalitions intending to contest the first parliamentary election must register and seek new accreditation with COMELEC through the BRAC. Failure to do so bars them from participating.

citizen_questions.q: Is the women's quota still there?
citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 3 expressly retains the requirement that at least 30% of a regional party's nominees be women, and as far as practicable one in every three.

citizen_questions.q: How much of the vote does a party need for a seat?
citizen_questions.a: At least two and one-half percent of the total valid votes cast for the party system election.
All of them were revoked and cancelled by Section 7. Organisations must go through a new certification process, and the certifying ministry has a non-extendible 15 days to act.

citizen_questions.q: What if the ministry sits on my application?
citizen_questions.a: The certification issues on the lapse of the 15-day period unless there is justifiable cause for denial, and failure to act within the period is a ground for disciplinary action against the official.

citizen_questions.q: How are Non-Moro Indigenous Peoples represented?
citizen_questions.a: Uniquely — their sectoral representative is elected by their own sectoral assembly, while other sectoral representatives are elected by direct plurality of votes.

citizen_questions.q: Do BTA members have to resign to run?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 16 provides that incumbent appointed BTA members whose positions are elective by nature are not deemed ipso facto resigned on filing a Certificate of Candidacy, and neither are Members holding Cabinet or other executive posts.
₱500 million is appropriated to augment COMELEC's funds, drawn from readily available Bangsamoro Government sources and released immediately.

display_header.what_this_does: Rewrites party and sectoral rules for the first parliamentary election and funds it with ₱500 million.
display_header.who_it_affects: Political parties · sectoral organisations · women candidates · every voter

views.simple: Amends the Bangsamoro Electoral Code ahead of the first parliamentary election: 5,000 members and region-wide chapters to form a party, a 2.5% threshold for party seats, a retained 30% women's quota, revocation of all sectoral certifications with a new 15-day process, and ₱500 million for COMELEC.
